email.subject: Your ThisIsTea password has been changed

body.v: The password for your ThisIsTea account has just been changed. If this was you, there is nothing else you need to do.
If you changed it because you had typed the old one into a dubious page, let your IT or security team know as well, and turn on multi-factor authentication in the app, under Security.

hotspots.explain: The address ends in thisistea.example, the real domain.
A plain confirmation: no threat, no deadline.
No link. The email points you to the app you already have.
Multi-factor authentication adds a second lock: a stolen password is no longer enough to get into your account.

who.prompt: Who is really writing to you? Read the address, not just the name.
who.answer: ThisIsTea, from its real domain: thisistea.example.
choices: A scammer with a near-identical address

emotion.prompt: Which feeling is this email pressing on?
emotion.answer: None. It is a confirmation, sent after you changed your password yourself.
choices: Panic over a break-in in progress

ask.prompt: What does it actually want you to do?
ask.answer: Nothing urgent. It only suggests telling the IT team and turning on multi-factor authentication if you were caught out.
choices: Click a link and sign in
Nothing, apart from good reflexes if you were caught out

verify.prompt: How can you check through a channel you control?
verify.answer: You have already done what was needed. If you clicked and typed your password earlier: change it from the real site, tell the IT team straight away and turn on multi-factor authentication. The faster you act, the less time the attacker has to use your login details.
choices: Delete the email and tell nobody
Wait a few days to see if anything happens
Change the password, tell IT, add a second lock

actions.label: Change the password from the real site and turn on multi-factor authentication
actions.consequence: A stolen password is no longer enough to get into your account.

actions.label: Report it to the IT team straight away
actions.consequence: If a colleague received the same trap, your report may stop them in time.

actions.label: Delete the email and say nothing: if nobody noticed, no harm done
actions.consequence: Your silence buys the attacker time. And the person at the next desk may have received the same email.

actions.label: Wait a few days to see whether anything strange happens
actions.consequence: Meanwhile, the attacker can use your login details.

attacker_reveal: A real service sends exactly this after a password change. If my fake link worked on you earlier, now is the moment to shut the door on me: new password, second lock, IT team told. Waiting in silence, on the other hand, gives me all the time I need.
